statement: clippy's doc_lazy_continuation lint fires on any doc-comment continuation line that BEGINS with `>` -- which includes the literal `>=1` shorthand (e.g. `/// carry >=1 test id`) once it wraps to a new `///`/`//!` line, because clippy reads the leading `>` as an unmarked blockquote continuation. `cargo clippy --fix` 'fixes' this by inserting a `> ` marker on the continuation line, which is syntactically valid but turns the sentence into an unintended nested blockquote rather than fixing the real issue.
why: h03's THREAT-MAP validators doc comments used `>=1` (threshold shorthand) repeatedly across multi-line list items; every line-wrap that happened to start with `>=1` tripped `-D warnings` clippy in CI, and the auto-fix produced a semantically wrong blockquote instead of prose.
howToApply: In any Rust doc comment (`///` or `//!`) in this workspace, never use the `>=N`/`<=N` shorthand where it could land at the start of a wrapped line -- write "at least N"/"at most N" in prose instead. This is purely a doc-comment concern; `>=1` inside a `format!`/string literal (i.e. actual Finding detail text) does NOT trigger the lint and is fine to keep.

statement: The legacy JS enforcer's `placeholder-implementation` check (SRC-1.2) flags the literal word `stub` anywhere in production source, including inside doc comments that use it in its ordinary English sense ('a manifest stub carried inline by a fixture') rather than as a TODO/incomplete-code marker. It has no context-awareness distinguishing 'this data shape is a deliberate simplified stand-in, documented as such' from 'this code is an unfinished placeholder'.
why: h03's THREAT_MAP module doc comments described the fixture-carried `moneyCriticalUnits` list as an 'h01-shaped money-critical manifest stub' (a genuine, intentional, fully-implemented design choice -- not incomplete code) and this word alone produced 4 SRC-1.2 violations under `ocentra_enforcer_check --check placeholder-implementation` even though `cargo clippy`/`cargo test` were fully green.
howToApply: When documenting an intentionally-simplified or inline-carried data shape in Rust doc comments anywhere in this workspace, avoid the bare word `stub` (and likely `placeholder`/`TODO`/`not-implemented` by the same mechanism) -- use `snapshot`, `inline copy`, or `simplified form` instead. Always dogfood-check (`ocentra_enforcer_check --check placeholder-implementation`) new doc-heavy modules before considering them done, since this is a real check the CI gate runs, not noise.

statement: h03's THREAT_MAP validators are the FIRST Track H validators in this workspace to operate over a JSON record (`ValidationInput.source` parsed as `serde_json`) rather than Rust/other source text via `syn`/text-scan, following h01's money_critical.rs pattern of returning `Vec::new()` silently on unparseable source rather than a Finding. The three rules (THREAT-MAP-UNIT-COVERAGE.1, THREAT-MAP-NO-UNMAPPED.1, THREAT-MAP-THREAT-HAS-TEST.1) share one deserialized `ThreatMap` struct/parse function but are otherwise fully independent validators -- each rule checks a distinct edge of the same record, which is why 3 separate fail/pass fixture pairs were needed (a fixture with a coverage gap on a PRESENT unit is different from a fixture with an ABSENT unit, which is different from a fixture with a threat that has zero backing tests).
why: Distinguishing 'unit present but incompletely mapped' (UNIT-COVERAGE) from 'unit absent from the map entirely' (NO-UNMAPPED) required minting a THIRD fixture pair (tests/fixtures/threat_test_mapping/mapped/bad/partial_mapping.json) beyond the two representative-triple fixture pairs the workpack's Acceptance And Proof section named -- the workpack's own `unmapped/bad/unit_absent.json` fixture, while it fails NO-UNMAPPED, is actually fully-mapped for the one unit it DOES list, so it would falsely pass UNIT-COVERAGE's own fail-fixture requirement if reused verbatim.
howToApply: Future h03-adjacent or Track-H JSON-record validators should mint one dedicated fail fixture per DISTINCT failure mode even when two rules superficially share the same input shape -- do not assume a fail fixture proving rule A also proves rule B just because they both fire on 'missing mapping data'; check what specific edge each rule inspects before reusing a fixture across rules.
